---
address: maldives.geo.postalCode
description: Real Maldivian postcodes — five digits, leading zeros kept. The structure is two digits of atoll zone and three of place: 02040 is in Haa Dhaalu, 19020 is Hithadhoo in Addu, 20026 is the head office of Maldives Post on Boduthakurufaanu Magu in Malé. The leading zero is not decoration and the ZERO ZERO is not a bug: Alif Dhaalu, the southern half of Ari Atoll, holds the whole 00 zone because it was created in 1984 after 01 to 19 had been handed out, so Mahibadhoo is 00040 and Dhangethi is 00060 and a postcode field typed as an integer silently deletes an atoll — see maldives.geo.postalCodeZone. Atoll codes are sparse and mostly end in 0, one per inhabited island or resort, stepping 010, 020, 030 through the atoll; Malé codes are dense and go down to the individual street, which is why more than half the values in this file are 20xxx. The list is what could be verified against published registers rather than every code in existence; Gaafu Alif, whose zone is 16 by position between Laamu at 15 and Gaafu Dhaalu at 17, had no island-level codes in any register consulted and is therefore represented by its zone alone and not by invented five-digit codes.
